newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN SAYS HE KNOWS OF NO TALKS ABOUT BULLS' PLANS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN SAYS HE KNOWS OF NO TALKS ABOUT BULLS' PLANS.

text.p: Michael Jordan, the calm eye at the centre of a swirl of reports of backroom talks to decide the future of the Chicago Bulls, claims he knows nothing about any such talks, in the backroom or the front.

The NBA's marquee player, even in the midst of trying to win a fifth championship, is most often questioned about whether he will be back next season. He has said he would not discuss a new contract with Bulls Chairman Jerry Reinsdorf and General Manager Jerry Krause until the season is over.
"Right now isn't a great time to deal with it," he said Tuesday after practice for Wednesday's Game 2 of the best-of-seven Finals, in which Chicago leads the Utah Jazz one game to none.
Jordan has announced some conditions for his return: he wants coach Phil Jackson back, he wants Scottie Pippen back.

When a reporter suggested that it appeared things were being worked out privately or in backrooms somewhere, Jordan said: "I don't know. You guys are doing all the talking, saying there's talking in the back room, talking in the front room. I don't know.

"If it is, great. I haven't had any conversations, because my job is to play the game of basketball. I haven't talked to Jerry, I haven't talked to my agent. The little conversation I've had with Phil -- it's coach/player relations."

Tuesday's Chicago Tribune, citing sources close to Jordan and management, reported Jordan would ask the Bulls for $36 million for next season, and that the club wanted him back -- perhaps for $33 million -- up from $30 million he was paid for this season.
The newspaper also said Jackson would be re-signed, Pippen would not be traded, for now anyway, but rebounding king and frequent bad actor Dennis Rodman would be let go.

When reporters asked Jordan how much money he would want next year, the Game 1 hero, 1996-97 Most Valuable Player runner-up and nine-time scoring champion asked: "Do I deserve a raise? I don't know, you've got to look at the year."
He said Krause would give him a post-season rating: "I'm waiting for my evaluation period."
Jordan agreed that the recent filling of several NBA coaching jobs made it more likely Jackson would be back -- but only if he decided to keep coaching and if the Bulls offered the right deal.
"I think Phil's commitment initiates my commitment. It initiates my conversation. So until Phil's situation is done, my conversation is null," said Jordan.
"I don't want to break in a new coach. I don't want him to come ask me what he should do. Because I'm not getting his check and he certainly isn't getting mine."

Jackson, under his unique one-year deal, has already been allowed to hear some attractive offers from other clubs -- including the Orlando Magic, who just signed Chuck Daly. But Jackson is not saying what he will do. "I think it should be private business," he said.

Krause has denied reports that the Bulls were discussing trading Pippen to the Philadelphia 76ers for guard Jerry Stackhouse and the second pick in the upcoming NBA draft. But Krause has not ruled out a future trade involving Pippen.
Pippen said he has been through so many trade rumours, it does not bother him anymore.
Jordan was asked if he would like to see the Bulls reassure Pippen they would keep him. "It's evident that ain't going to happen," Jordan said.
"No matter what I would like. A lot of things haven't been done. Jerry's already said let's wait and see. I'm not going to twist his arm or hold a gun to his head. That's not my business to do."

Asked how he thought things would all turn out, Jordan said: "I've always been positive. I think everything stays in place until we as individuals, as a team start to break down and become unsuccessful."
Rodman may have gotten one suspension or one new hair colour too many for Chicago management's liking, but he would like to stay.

"Of course," he said. "Who wouldn't? It would be stupid to say I wouldn't want to come back. I love Chicago, so if they want me back, great. Phil wants me back so hopefully that can carry some weight down the line."
Rodman, who has won NBA crowns with both the Bulls and the Detroit Pistons, would not want to go to a rebuilding team.
"I'm going on 37 years old. I don't need to start with a young team. If I can go to a team and win another championship, great. If I'm here, I'd love to win another championship."
